page: Microsoft Azure ND96isr_H200_v5 is an isolated, GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for extreme compute and deep learning workloads. The instance is powered by 96 dedicated x86_64 Intel vCPUs alongside 1,850 GB of system memory, providing approximately 19.27 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by eight NVIDIA Hopper H200 GPUs delivering an aggregate of 1,128 GB of high-bandwidth GPU memory.

For data-intensive processing, the instance integrates 31,820 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The host runs on Microsoft Hyper-V with dedicated CPU allocation and supports RDMA networking as well as Premium Storage. It allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring configured virtual network routing for external connectivity.

The concentration of eight NVIDIA H200 accelerators, 1.8 TB of system memory, and over 31 TB of local NVMe storage provides massive resource density on a single node, maximizing compute throughput for large-scale AI training, distributed LLM inference, and high-performance computing tasks. However, this high level of hardware aggregation represents an enterprise-tier investment that would be economically inefficient for non-accelerated or standard compute workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure ND96isr_H200_v5 is a high-density, GPU-accelerated instance designed for large-scale artificial intelligence and compute workloads. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, the instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs and 1,850 GB of system memory, achieving an allocation of 19.27 GB of RAM per vCPU. Acceleration is handled by eight NVIDIA Hopper H200 GPUs featuring a combined 1,128 GB of VRAM. For local data caching and high-throughput input/output, the instance incorporates 31,820 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside RDMA networking capabilities under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. With zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included, networking must be explicitly provisioned. ND96isr_H200_v5 is tailored for large language model pre-training, complex distributed AI inference, and intensive deep learning pipelines that require substantial GPU memory bandwidth and rapid local storage access.
